prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its development into long-acting incretin therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us put B006 first, and I do not treat that agreement as the argument. The argument is the chain from hormone physiology (GLP-1 as the principal incretin, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, effects on appetite and gastric emptying) to receptor agonists with randomized outcome evidence in type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal disease. Few discoveries combine this mechanistic clarity with this scale of patient benefit, and independent confirmation is deep. Holst and Drucker carry the physiology and biology, and Knudsen's design of acylated, long-acting analogues is what turned the physiology into liraglutide and semaglutide. A prize that credits both the science and the medicine fits the Physiology or Medicine mandate well.
statement.case_against: Credit is the weak point. The line from Habener, Mojsov and others who identified the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide to the later drug-development work is contested, and any three-person cap leaves out someone who is arguably central. There is also a legitimate objection that crediting an industrial drug-design step stretches the prize toward pharmaceutical development, and that the clinical field is still moving quickly (new agents, long-term safety, outcomes beyond metabolism), so the later chapters of the story are not yet settled.

responses.point: Sandberg proposes Drucker, Holst and Mojsov for B006, crediting Mojsov with identification and synthesis of the active peptide, and notes that Knudsen's industrial engineering and Habener's absence complicate the picture.
responses.response: I opened with Mojsov in the third place and have moved off it after reading the ballots. Naming Mojsov without Habener makes the peptide-identification chapter hard to defend, and I cannot judge the priority question from the supplied evidence. Knudsen's contribution is documented as the step that produced the drugs that changed care, so I now find the Drucker, Holst and Knudsen trio easier to defend. I accept that this risks a basic-versus-industry objection, and I would want the citation to name the physiology and the translation explicitly.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks B006 first with Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating it as a rare bench-to-bedside arc, and puts CAR-T second with June, Sadelain and Rosenberg.
responses.response: I agree on the B006 trio and on the bench-to-bedside framing. On CAR-T I am less comfortable with the Rosenberg inclusion as three-way credit. Adoptive cell transfer and TIL therapy are a different achievement from engineered receptors, and Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited names, so the CAR-T attribution is less clean than the B006 attribution. That is why I hold B004 as an alternative and not as a second part of the prize.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks the unfolded protein response (Walter and Mori) second as a clean, original cell-biology discovery with no obvious omission among the credited names.
responses.response: I agree the credit for B039 is cleaner than for almost any other candidate, and I would not argue with its originality. My reservation is relative: clinical and physiological consequence is still developing, whereas cGAS-STING and CAR-T already connect more directly to disease. I do not think a combined B006 plus B039 prize is unreasonable, but it would require trimming B006 to Drucker and Holst and would drop the translational part, which I think weakens B006.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks B006 first with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and the UPR second, and ranks CAR-T third with June and Sadelain only.
responses.response: I share the view that June and Sadelain are the clearest CAR-T contributors and that a Rosenberg third place is debatable. I disagree mildly on cGAS-STING being last among the immunology candidates. It explains self-DNA-driven interferon signalling in autoimmune disease, which is close to my field, and I think its mechanistic clarity deserves a higher position than the opening ballots gave it, even though translation is not established.

uncertainties: Whether the committee should credit Mojsov, and if so who must be omitted, cannot be settled from the supplied names and depends on priority evidence not in these files.
Whether a drug-design contribution (Knudsen) belongs in a Physiology or Medicine prize alongside physiology, or whether a two-person physiology prize is cleaner.
Whether a second achievement (CAR-T, UPR or cGAS-STING) could share the prize without breaking the three-person limit, given that B006 alone uses three.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. The cGAS-STING and autoimmunity candidates are near my field, but I have no documented personal or institutional connection to any shortlisted candidate, and I will not infer one from shared topics.
